successors.name: Kushan Empire
successors.text: Bactria and the five xihou, united when 'the Kushana, become dominant' (c.

capitals.name: Court north of the Gui (Oxus), city not named

ledger.x: 404 BCE: the Yuezhi hold the Hexi Corridor between Dunhuang and Qilian.
203 BCE: Modu's war on the Yuezhi.
178 BCE: the Xiongnu overrun the Tarim and eastern Xinjiang.
176 BCE: the Xiongnu drive the Yuezhi from Hexi.
176 BCE: the Yuezhi lose the Hexi Corridor and their king.
165 BCE: the Yuezhi settle the Ili valley.
132 BCE: the Wusun take the Ili.
130 BCE: the Yuezhi settle Sogdia and the north bank of the Oxus.
126 BCE: Bactria south of the Oxus comes 'under their sway'.
42: Kujula Kadphises' Kushans absorb the five xihou.

wars.name: Xiongnu–Yuezhi wars
wars.outcome: Xiongnu victory: three wars (under Touman; 203 BCE; 'before or in 176 BCE'); the Yuezhi king killed and the Yuezhi driven from Hexi in 176 BCE; Modu's letter of 174 BCE claims to have wiped them out.

wars.name: Wusun conquest of the Ili
wars.outcome: Wusun victory: the Yuezhi driven from the Ili to Sogdia and Bactria; the Wusun settle the Ili.

wars.name: Yuezhi conquest of Bactria
wars.outcome: Yuezhi victory: Bactria 'came under their sway' by 126 BCE; the Greco-Bactrian kingdom disestablished c.

certainty.note: Nomadic ranges throughout: the Hexi homeland, the Ili valley and the Oxus lands are approximate; the Oxus itself is the one natural line (Zhang Qian's north bank/south bank).
